item.text: {"summary":"Fix zero padding between 128-bit integer output chunks.","explanation":"Both failure groups come from the same formatter in `absl/numeric/int128.cc`. In the octal and hexadecimal multi-chunk cases in `Uint128.OStreamValueTest` and `Int128.OStreamValueTest`, the tests compare `os.str()` with `test_case.expected`. For example, the octal case expects `\"1000000000000000000000\"`, but `os.str()` is `\"1                    0\"`; the hex case expects `\"8000000000000000\"`, but `os.str()` is `\"8              0\"`. `Uint128ToFormattedString` pads lower chunks to the fixed chunk width using a space fill, inserting spaces into the digit sequence. Using a zero fill preserves the required chunk width and produces contiguous digits for both signed and unsigned stream output.","edits":[{"path":"absl/numeric/int128.cc","old":"    os << std::noshowbase << std::setfill(' ') << std::setw(div_base_log);","new":"    os << std::noshowbase << std::setfill('0') << std::setw(div_base_log);"}]}
